correctness.rationale: The normalized quadratic Dirichlet tilt, digamma recurrence, entropy first moment, and complete cross-moment expression are reconstructed in the proof. Subtracting the means yields the stated weighted covariance decomposition. Strict digamma monotonicity and strictly positive pair mass establish negativity for every positive real parameter vector. A separate symbolic three-variable identity check and exact-fraction checks for integer configurations agree; finite checks are supplementary, not substitutes for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the full asymmetric finite-Dirichlet Shannon/Simpson cross-covariance identity and its heterogeneity decomposition, strict sign, sharp equality condition, and fixed-total concentration reversal. The inspected relevant works furnish means/variances of one diversity index or a symmetric Dirichlet subfamily, not this cross-index identity or its implications. Targeted semantic and text searches disclosed no stronger result implying the theorem; priority is not claimed exhaustive.
residual_risks: Priority searches were targeted, not a systematic review of all historical Bayesian-diversity moment literature.
An algebraically equivalent expression might exist under a different normalization, notation, or entropy family; no independent audit has taken place.

value.rationale: Shannon entropy and Simpson concentration are two standard, differently rare-species-sensitive biodiversity statistics. Joint uncertainty under unequal finite Dirichlet priors is not resolved by their marginal means or variances. The closed-form theorem gives an all-parameter sign that would otherwise be unclear for asymmetric priors, isolates an explicitly nonnegative heterogeneity correction with exact equality case, and shows by natural fixed-total comparison that asymmetry can strengthen the magnitude. These are structural facts useful for joint Bayesian diversity uncertainty, not a renamed textbook scalar moment or arbitrary numerical slice.
